turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.
"The end of it." Okay. That's a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says never to use it as the only basis for punishing a student. What else do you have?
I don't need more proof than that.

"Don't need more." I'm writing that down. Your own procedure, 4.3, says software alone doesn't establish a concern, and 4.2 says you call the parent before any mark goes in. Nobody called me, Hale, so withdraw the zero.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
My child never lies. Are you calling me a liar, Hale? Because I'm writing that sentence down word for word, and the principal will be reading it.

"Zero stands." Okay. No call home, no conversation with Owen, and a software score you can't show me, so that's the whole file. I'll want that in an email from you today, because the next person you say it to is the principal.
